paragraphs: Chapter 1139
Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (8)
With his back to the bloated sun, which felt as if it were trampling the sky, Kelliark grinned.
This fight was fun.
Those who should have been easily broken were holding on for a surprisingly long time, and just when it seemed to be over, something new would begin. They would grow stronger, and they would endure.

[Well, you're misunderstanding. I am just enjoying myself, Jin Runcandel... After my victory, all that will be left is something boring and empty anyway. Will someone like you ever appear again? Will all dimensions be manipulated to my liking, and then will I too, like the creators, encounter an error like myself or you? That day is far off, so isn't this a moment worth celebrating?]
Barisada was burning white. Kelliark's Origin Stone, which had transformed into a staff, also shimmered brilliantly with a golden light.
'I can remain human...'
The power of light.
Before knowing its true nature, Jin had a gut feeling that if he took the legacy, he might become something other than human.
If the power of light left by Solderet hadn't been, as Kelliark had said, a 'very small authority', that would surely have been the case.

But the power Jin had obtained was finite. It allowed him to handle light only for a limited time. That was why, even though he could stand against the full power of the Sun God and the Origin Stone, Jin did not have the power to restore the already broken world.
There were people left.

He was not an opponent he could fight while thinking about the aftermath. Cut. Jin did not forget his essence as a martial artist. With the sole intention of cutting down the enemy, Jin moved forward.
The flashing blade created afterimages in Kelliark's vision.
A speed that could not be read even with the eyes of a god, let alone a human. Every time the light flashed, a part of Kelliark's body was cut.
Without insight, foresight, manipulation, and distortion, it would have been impossible to respond.
[But, it's an amusing thing. Solderet realized he was light too late. If he had known from the beginning, it would have been better for him to fight me directly.]
"There are many things in this world that cannot be done without sacrifice. It's not something you, who have filled your desires only by trampling on everything, can understand."
Kiiiik!
Barisada and the Origin Stone tangled and scraped against each other. Behind them, the red sea was creating a tidal wave, trying to swallow the people again.
But more light than that left flashes across the entire battlefield, tearing the tidal wave to shreds.
When Kelliark tried to manipulate history, Jin stabbed his sword at his head, and when he tried to distort space, he fixed a single ray of light in that place.
Neither the power of the Origin Stone nor the authority of Kinzelo could penetrate that light. Just as it is impossible to hold light in both hands and change it at will.
Right now, only Jin could do that.
'His power is slowly being worn down.'
It was subtle.
But every time he cut Kelliark with Barisada, Jin could feel with his whole body that his power was weakening, albeit minutely.
Of course, Kelliark would manipulate himself each time to make the damage as if it hadn't happened, but that was by no means an eternal cycle.
[You're obsessed with fighting like a human. For someone who has the form of a ball of light.]
Although he clearly looked like light, Kelliark kept feeling as if a sword was entering his body.

On the contrary, because he had obtained too much authority, he could not see Jin's true nature. He could not see the fact that he was just a human who got tired when he moved his body and became dull when he bled.
That was the reason why Jin could push Kelliark back now.
Reading the situation on the battlefield and sending light accordingly was, in the end, the sense of a Genesis Knight, not an act that relied on the authority of a god like Kelliark.
Jin was hiding his ragged breathing that was rising up to his chin.
He had to hide it. He couldn't show any signs of fatigue until he cut him down. It wasn't that difficult.
Because the people were waking up.
The people who had been manipulated by Kelliark's desire were coming to their senses, and those who had been madly pointing their swords at each other were now checking their opponents' wounds.
They felt sorrow looking at their dead comrades and suffered feeling the world that had been irreparably destroyed.
Compared to that, fighting with the borrowed power of light was certainly an easy task.
When spears fell from the sun, he parried them. When a space explosion occurred, he dodged it. And the staff that Kelliark swung himself, he deflected.
He struck down with all his might.
From the sky to the ground, a single streak of light extending from Barisada left a long, huge trajectory. Crack. A small cracking sound was heard from the Origin Stone.
The tip of the staff split open, and a crimson liquid like blood poured out from within. Kelliark's body was also bisected, and his regeneration slowed.

It was still fast enough to be the blink of an eye, but it had definitely slowed. Instead, Kelliark, while regenerating, simultaneously thrust his hand into the center of the ball of light that was Jin.
The Light-Heart shattered and the center of his chest was pierced.

But in an instant, the light that had spread throughout the entire battlefield gathered into it and filled the hole in his chest, and Jin was using the remaining light from that to unfold a new sword technique.
Runcandel Magic Sword Secret Technique.
Sun-Slicer.
The sword that Temar had created in the past to cut down Solderet.

At that time, not only Temar but also Solderet himself did not know who he was. Therefore, the sword, which had been devised in vague preparation for when Solderet would be reverted to a Sun God by the Zipples, was now aiming for Kelliark's sun.
The giant trajectory left by Barisada began to rotate.
The pure white circle created by one rotation instantly swallowed the sun, dyeing the entire sky in a dazzling light.
[Hah!]

It was the authority of Kinzelo, which he had finally grasped after traveling all dimensions. But Kelliark had to confirm that even if he raised his authority again, the sun could not break through the light and appear.
Was it a power that couldn't even overcome this much light?
It was absurd.
The power of Kinzelo was truly whole. With that alone, without the Origin Stone, he could create and destroy the world.
In contrast, the light Jin had obtained was a handful.
It would be appropriate to call it a handful. That small power was completely covering the sun.
That was why he coveted it more and more.

But how could he take the light? Kelliark had been harboring such a question throughout the fight. The light that was not manipulated by the Origin Stone, that could not be grasped with both hands, how on earth could he take it?
No answer came to mind.
'As soon as I become the one true god, there are more incomprehensible things than when I was human...'
Unpleasant.
Moreover, the sun was not just buried in the light, but was being continuously split by something within it.
Kelliark thought that too was light.
But it was a sword. It was the will of the martial artist named Jin Runcandel. Kelliark still couldn't know that fact.
He just thought that Jin was fighting with a superior power that had never existed in the world before.
The ragged breath he had been holding in was inevitably spewed out, his grip on the sword was trembling, and his two legs felt like they could collapse at any time.
Kelliark could not see the form of a human at all. The weak reality that he could kill more easily than crushing a bug, if only he knew.

[How does it feel, Jin Runcandel? To be honest, at this point, the feeling of absurdity is greater than the feeling of joy for me. If I had known there was such a power, I wouldn't have had a reason to obsess over Kinzelo.]
"You're just babbling on about how you think you're going to lose to me."
[Haha, is that how it sounds? Well, I'll say you're half right.]
It seems I can't win.
Kelliark was doubting himself. At first, it was just surprising that he could fight on equal terms, but now he clearly felt that the power of light was superior.
It was almost funny how his inner self was changing with every passing second.

While they were talking for a moment, his body had been cut dozens of times. The sun, covered by the light, could no longer drop even a small amount of heat, let alone a spear, on Jin, and the enemies were escaping death.
No one was dying anymore.

There was no one floundering in the sea, no one suffering from manipulation and distortion. From Laprarosa, the priests were even coming down directly to look after the wounded, and the golden fleet was circling the battlefield and recovering the fallen.
In other words, they were acting as if they were fighting against a human, not a one true god. When he swung the Origin Stone, annoyed by the sight, the light invariably blocked him.
It was irritating.
However, Kelliark was comforted by the fact that in one area at least, he was overwhelming Jin.
Destroying the world.
[I am dealing with you quite easily, but you can't pay any attention to the outside of the battlefield.]
Jin's eyes narrowed.
As he said, Jin couldn't stop the entire red sea that was flooding the whole world. Although light existed everywhere, it wasn't that Jin could control all of that light.
"So, you're saying it's your victory in the end if you just destroy this whole world?"

[That story has already been established. From the looks of it, you don't have the power to rebuild this land. You're tying down my sun, but you haven't fundamentally annihilated Kinzelo's authority. And you... don't have much time left. The time you can handle light.]
Kelliark had grasped the greatest weakness of the light Jin possessed. Jin didn't answer and just stared at him.
In fact, the more he cut Kelliark, the more Jin was aware of the light leaving him.

[It's not eternal, but it is short, and above all, intense. It suits you perfectly. It's like seeing the life of a special human. Finite and infinite, it seems to have been proven which of the two has more value. I can't win against you in this state... If so, then I too will become finite.]
The sun energy was disappearing from Kelliark's body.
He had discarded it. He was making the power of the Sun God Kinzelo, which he had finally obtained, leave him.
A moment later, he was looking at Jin again, with the appearance of an ordinary human.
He could see not a ball of light, but an injured human, barely standing against him.
"Ah... yes. Now I can see again how weak you were."
